Substitution in morphism expressions

The Segal section uses composition in a common parameter category. The supporting calculation is that restriction and changes of endpoints preserve the chosen composite, with its endpoint data.

Write \(\operatorname {Ar}(C)=\Fun ([1],C)\), with endpoint evaluations \(e_0,e_1\). A morphism expression from \(x\) to \(y\), for \(x,y\colon \Gamma \to C\), consists of \(A\colon \Gamma \to \operatorname {Ar}(C)\) and frames \(p\colon e_0A=x\), \(q\colon e_1A=y\). An endpoint-preserving comparison from \((A,p,q)\) to \((A',p',q')\) is an identification \(\eta \colon A=A'\) together with \[ p'\cdot (e_0\star \eta )=p,\qquad q'\cdot (e_1\star \eta )=q. \] Retargeting along \(a\colon x=x'\) and \(b\colon y=y'\) replaces the frames \(p,q\) by \(a\cdot p,b\cdot q\) and leaves the arrow family unchanged. We use \(\star \) for whiskering and \(\cdot \) for vertical composition, rightmost factor first. All categories involved are fixed absolute categories.

Supplementary Lemma 1. For \(r\colon \Delta \to \Gamma \), restriction takes endpoint-preserving comparisons to endpoint-preserving comparisons. The restricted arrow is \(Ar\) and its source frame is \[ (p\star r)\cdot \alpha _{r,A,e_0}^{-1}\colon e_0(Ar)=xr, \] with the analogous formula at the target. Here \(\alpha _{r,A,e_0}\colon (e_0A)r=e_0(Ar)\) is the associator.

Proof idea

Restrict the underlying comparison to \(\eta \star r\). Whisker each endpoint equation by \(r\) and use compatibility of whiskering with vertical composition and the associator. The inverse associators in the displayed frames convert the result to exactly the endpoint equations for the restricted expressions. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Restricting an expression by \(\mathrm {id}_{\Gamma }\) and retargeting its endpoints by the right unitors gives an endpoint-preserving comparison to the original expression. For \(r\colon \Delta \to \Gamma \) and \(s\colon \Theta \to \Delta \), successive restriction by \(r\) and \(s\), retargeted by \(\alpha _{s,r,x}\) and \(\alpha _{s,r,y}\), compares with restriction by \(r\circ s\).

Proof idea

Use the right unitor of \(A\) for the first underlying arrow comparison, and \(\alpha _{s,r,A}\) for the second. Their endpoint equations are the unit and successive-substitution equations for transport through a fixed functor \(e_0\) or \(e_1\). The finite unitor and associator compatibility calculations, derived from the pentagon and triangle, establish these equations while retaining the given frames. These are the same product-calculus comparisons discussed in Pairing and precomposition. □

Supplementary Lemma 3. Assume the Segal axiom. For composable expressions \(f\colon x\to y\), \(g\colon y\to z\), and \(r\colon \Delta \to \Gamma \), there is an endpoint-preserving comparison \[ (g|_r)\circ (f|_r)\simeq (g\circ f)|_r. \] If \(a\colon x=x'\), \(b\colon y=y'\), and \(c\colon z=z'\) change the endpoints, composing the retargeted expressions compares with retargeting \(g\circ f\) by \(a,c\).

Proof idea

A presentation of \(g\circ f\) consists of its chosen triangle, comparisons of the short edges with \(f,g\), and the long edge with the composite. It includes compatibility at all three vertices. Restrict this entire presentation by \(r\). The endpoint calculation of Supplementary Lemma 1 supplies its new boundary comparisons. It is now a presentation of \((g\circ f)|_r\) as a composite of \(f|_r,g|_r\). Recognition of composites through the Segal equivalence compares it with the chosen composite of those inputs.

For retargeting, change the three vertex frames and retain the triangle. The common change \(b\) at the middle vertex occurs on both short edges; its compatibility is retained in the new presentation. Apply the same recognition argument. The comparison preserves the two outer endpoints. □

These lemmas provide the individual substitution comparisons used in specializing the unit and associativity arguments. They do not assert an additional coherence theorem for all choices of Segal inverses.
